reasoning_checks: Node short rate is known before the next interval; coupons are added once at their actual next payment date and final continuation is zero after the final payment. Unit-face bond prices, 100-face claim multiplier and CU funding are distinguished.

Full-path bank account uses actual prior rate history. LH and HL reach the same date2 rate node but have bank wealth1000/969 and1000/931; Arrow aggregation retains their different prices. Normalized Arrow weights are not silently equated with bank-account Q probabilities.

Positive d and strictly positive conditional P/Q support yield an equivalent pricing representation. Predictable finite self-financing discounted wealth is a Q martingale by linearity and conditional expectation; nonnegative positive-somewhere terminal wealth contradicts zero initial expectation.

The selected positive pricing law does not prove that all terminal state indicators are attainable or uniquely priced. The proof concerns stipulated consistently priced assets and trading rights; arbitrary unspanned terminal claims are explicitly excluded from a uniqueness claim.

Each calibration level has a strictly positive denominator and is unique only after shape and Q choices. The imposed s<1/2 bound is specific to t=0,1,2. Earlier discount prices do not depend on later fitted levels. Nonmonotone positive curves remain allowed when external costless storage is absent.

P changes alter forecasts, SDF and expected holding returns while leaving a fixed Q pricing model unchanged. Returns use actual purchase/sale dates and include no maturity payment at an earlier sale. Local expected-excess/covariance identities are exact at all displayed nodes.

The forward is a harmonic aggregation of gross next short rates. Jensen gives its gap from the Q arithmetic mean; that averaging gap is separated from a P/Q change. The chapter does not label every forward-minus-forecast difference a pure holding-return premium.

Finite additive mean-reversion moments follow an explicitly iterated recursion and independent unit-variance innovations. Phi1 is discussed through the finite sum, not a zero denominator. The physical AR case is separate from curve calibration and can fail to recombine.

Exponentiating the rate imposes positive rates and declining D. Finite square-root-scaled updates need their own state-domain check; clamping changes the mean from.008 to.0115 in the original counterexample. No continuous-time positivity result is assumed.

The nonlinear contract pays cash only at date1. Its hedge liquidates the date2 zero then repays its date0 bank borrowing. Distinct successor bond prices make the two-equation system full rank. At zero dispersion equal claim payments are replicated with a bank-only choice instead of dividing by zero.

All three tree families fit the supplied curve but value the original contract at.92,1.41 and2.36. Frozen base hedge errors in the wide model have priced loss-.95 equal to the initial price gap, so this is model mismatch rather than an alleged arbitrage within a single unchanged model.

Discount-coordinate scenarios recalibrate every affected level. The conditional derivative51 in D2 is distinct from the future-date bond hedge coefficient1410/19. At D2=.92 both payment branches are zero; extrapolating the interior derivative to-.12 is explicitly rejected.

The wide negative short rate still has a positive gross bank return. Adding costless storage changes rights and creates the explicit conditional borrowing/storage arbitrage; this is not smuggled into the original model.

Research critique separates calibration residuals, expectations estimation, conventions and holdout hedge evaluation. Original synthetic fixtures are never represented as October2026 observations; dated source discussion does not authenticate current rates or fitted coefficients.
